sections.h2: What should a seller know about Reynoldsburg's size and housing?
sections.html:
Reynoldsburg is a Columbus suburb with a large retail base and a mix of owners and renters. Federal estimates for July 2025 show 43,350 people, 5.5% more than the 2020 base of 41,074, living on 11.12 square miles of land in 17,280 households.

Wikipedia says the area was first settled in 1802 and platted in 1831 as Frenchtown, and the present name was fixed in 1893. Local pride centers on the tomato: the city bills itself the Birthplace of the Tomato, and its festival has run each August since 1965. Blacklick Creek runs through town, and Blacklick Woods, a 643-acre Metro Park that opened in 1948 as the first in Franklin County, lies within the city.

Three numbers frame pricing: 61.6% of homes are owner-occupied, the midpoint value is $244,300 and the midpoint rent is $1,259.

sections.h2: Why do three counties touch Reynoldsburg?
sections.html:
The city reaches into Franklin, Fairfield and Licking counties, each with a separate auditor and treasurer. Council legislation from 2026 mentions a Taylor Road annexation in Etna Township and Summit Road work shared with Licking County, so a parcel near that edge may answer to a different office.

City council resolutions for 2026 show how this works in practice: the clerk certifies nuisance costs to both the Franklin County Auditor and the Licking County Auditor for collection, and the city certifies its tax levies to both. If the city ever billed you for cleanup on the lot, ask which county auditor holds the charge before closing.

sections.h2: What does the Reynoldsburg Building Department require?
sections.html:
The Building Division administers four codes, Ohio Building, Residential, Property Maintenance and Flood Damage Prevention, plus the National Electrical Code, and it issues certificates of occupancy and permits for building, electrical, heating, plumbing, sign, sidewalk and flood hazard work. It sits at 7232 East Main Street and answers at 614-322-6802.

  • Residential plan review starts with a permit application, construction drawings and a $100 non-refundable deposit.
  • Plumbing plan review and inspection run through Franklin County Public Health, at 280 East Broad Street in Columbus, not through the city.
  • Contractors register each year with a $75 fee, proof of liability coverage of at least $500,000 and a state license where one applies.
  • Inspections requested by 3 p.m. through the automated line, 614-322-6821, are generally done the next business day, though the city has up to four days.

Inspectors working for buyers tend to ask about permits for decks, basement finishes and plumbing changes, so gather those records early.

The city's 2026 legislation page lists an ordinance to establish Section 705, Permitting Short-Term Rentals, as a chapter of the codified ordinances. An owner who rents a house by the night, and wants to sell it to another host, should ask the city whether any permit passes to a new owner.

The same list shows a council action in 2026 to expand the Eastern Community Reinvestment Area, which allows property tax abatement, and several agreements for tax exemption on new projects. Ask the city whether your address sits inside an abatement district before you tell a buyer an abatement is available.

sections.h2: Who works and shops in Reynoldsburg, and does it help a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, since local jobs feed buyer demand. Wikipedia draws on the city's 2021 audit, which names Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works companies, Reynoldsburg City Schools, Kroger, Walmart and the State of Ohio among the biggest employers. The Ohio Department of Agriculture, the Ohio Fire Academy and the Office of the State Fire Marshal are also based in the city.

QuickFacts reports 2022 retail sales of about $1.69 billion, or $41,071 per resident, which is far above the other three cities in its comparison. The median household earns $72,972, commutes average 25.2 minutes, and 68.7% of residents aged 16 and up are in the labor force. A listing can point to nearby shopping and a manageable drive without naming a subdivision.

sections.h2: How do Reynoldsburg schools and parks shape listings?
sections.html:
The majority of the city is in Reynoldsburg City Schools, which Wikipedia says runs seven elementary schools, two junior highs and a high school with two campuses, Livingston and Summit. The city's parks department manages 275 acres of parkland across nine major parks, in addition to Blacklick Woods.

Buyers searching online often filter by school, so name the buildings that serve your street, such as Herbert Mills, Rosehill or Slate Ridge Elementary, only after you have confirmed the attendance zone with the district.

sections.h2: What checklist helps before you list a Reynoldsburg house?
sections.html:
A short list of calls and records can shorten the sale, whichever route you choose.

  • Confirm the county on your tax bill and the date of the next installment.
  • Pull permits for every deck, basement, furnace or plumbing change, and ask Franklin County Public Health about any plumbing approval.
  • Ask the Building Department about open code violation notices or citations on the address.
  • Check for a nuisance charge that the city sent to the county auditor.
  • Write down which Reynoldsburg elementary and junior high serve the street.

These answers also help a direct buyer make a firmer offer, because fewer unknowns remain at the closing table.

sections.h2: What should you know about Franklin County tax bills on a Reynoldsburg sale?
sections.html:
Franklin County set collection dates of March 2, 2026 and July 20, 2026 for the 2025 tax year, and payments after July 20 carry penalty and interest, the Treasurer says. Values are reset on a six-year cycle with a midpoint update, and between cycles they move only for physical changes, demolition or a Board of Revision ruling.

An owner disputing the 2026 value can file with the Auditor from November 20, 2026 until March 31, 2027. Qualifying owners who are 65, disabled or certain surviving spouses may use the Homestead credit, and the Auditor says its decision follows verification that total income does not exceed $41,000. The Treasurer's office, 614-525-3438, gives the amount owed on a given parcel.

sections.h2: Which Reynoldsburg sellers choose a cash sale?
sections.html:
Owners with deferred repairs, an unclosed permit or a departing tenant often pick it, because they value a set closing date over a long listing period. A buyer with a loan brings an appraisal and an inspection, and either can delay a sale or prompt repair requests.

Direct buyers typically take the house as-is. Get each offer in writing, learn who pays closing costs and read the settlement statement before signing day.

faqs.a: Reynoldsburg lies in Franklin, Fairfield and Licking counties, according to Wikipedia. Check your parcel to see which county auditor and treasurer bill your property.

faqs.q: Who handles plumbing permits in Reynoldsburg?
faqs.a: Franklin County Public Health reviews plumbing plans and schedules plumbing inspections for the city, per the city's Building Department page. Once a plan is approved, the permit application goes to the city's Building Division.

The city's 2026 legislation list includes an ordinance establishing Section 705, Permitting Short-Term Rentals. Ask the city for the current permit rules before listing a house that is used as a rental.

faqs.q: When was the second half of the 2025 Franklin County tax bill due?
faqs.a: July 20, 2026. After that date the Treasurer adds penalty and interest, and not receiving a bill does not change that.
The 2020 to 2024 count is 17,280 households with 2.38 people each on average. Roughly 61.6% are owned by the people living in them.
